title: Yemen Country Climate and Development Report: Policy Note
geographic_coverage: Yemen, national with spatial exposure and sector modelling
temporal_coverage: Recent baseline with projections mainly to 2050 and economic scenarios to 2040.
methodology: Climate and macroeconomic modelling, spatial exposure analysis, and sector policy synthesis.
limitations: Scenario results are not forecasts; the PDF contains erroneous West Bank and Gaza running headers and substantial data gaps. Reuse terms identified in the publisher catalog: CC BY-NC 3.0 IGO.

title: Charting the Course: A Water Security Diagnostic for Yemen
geographic_coverage: Yemen, national with basin and city cases including Taiz
temporal_coverage: Structural history and conflict-era evidence through 2024.
methodology: Administrative and remote-sensing evidence, mobile survey, literature synthesis, modelling, and consultations with nearly 1,700 participants.
limitations: Hydrological monitoring is degraded, groundwater information is incomplete, and consultation evidence is not a causal estimate. The full PDF exceeded the browser extraction limit; indexed primary text was inspected for the Foreword, Executive Summary, section 3.1.1 at printed p. 61, and section 6.2.3. The cited institutional passage at printed pp. 95-111 was not inspected, so the dependent evidence record was excluded.

title: Yemen's NDC 3.0 Vision
organization: Republic of Yemen and United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
temporal_coverage: Historical climate 1971-2020, mid-century projections, and policy roadmap through 2035.
methodology: Official climate-risk and policy synthesis with sector goals and institutional roadmap.
limitations: The registered document calls itself a Vision and says final NDC preparation and submission would occur in 2026; operational status is unclear.

title: Water-related Conflict Assessment Report
geographic_coverage: Selected districts in Abyan, Hadramawt, and Dhamar
temporal_coverage: Field and project evidence mainly from 2022-2023.
methodology: Local conflict assessment, interviews, community consultation, institutional analysis, and project-linked field evidence.
limitations: Narrow local coverage and project-linked evidence without independent measurement of durable conflict reduction. Originally published April 2022; updated September 2023; PDF copyright 2024. The publication states that reproduction requires prior permission.

title: Climate, Peace and Security Fact Sheet: Yemen 2023
organization: Stockholm International Peace Research Institute and Norwegian Institute of International Affairs
geographic_coverage: Yemen, national with selected local examples
methodology: Four-page secondary synthesis of climate, livelihood, mobility, and conflict pathways.
limitations: Secondary and concise; it identifies conditional mechanisms rather than demonstrating causal climate-conflict effects.

title: Climate and Health Vulnerability Assessment: Republic of Yemen
temporal_coverage: Recent baseline with CMIP6 projections to mid-century.
methodology: Desktop health-vulnerability assessment using CCKP and CMIP6 climate indicators, facility data, and adaptive-capacity indicators.
limitations: Facility exposure does not establish structural vulnerability or service failure; some labels and units appear inconsistent.

title: Yemen, Government-Controlled Areas: Acute Food Insecurity Analysis, March-December 2026
geographic_coverage: 118 districts in 12 Government of Yemen-controlled governorates
methodology: IPC convergence-of-evidence classification using food security, livelihoods, prices, assistance, conflict, and hazard evidence.
limitations: Medium evidence level and partial territorial coverage; results are multi-causal and not attributable to climate alone. The full report is dated 23 June 2026; the associated snapshot and IPC portal were released on 21 May 2026.

title: Independent Country Programme Evaluation: Yemen
organization: United Nations Development Programme Independent Evaluation Office
geographic_coverage: Yemen with fieldwork in seven governorates
methodology: Independent evaluation using document review, 169 interviews, more than 25 visits, and 13 focus groups.
limitations: No focus groups in de facto authority areas and limited causal attribution of welfare, resilience, or peace outcomes.

title: Inter-Agency Humanitarian Evaluation of the Yemen Crisis
geographic_coverage: Yemen with six-governorate survey and field evidence
methodology: Independent theory-based evaluation with 144 interviews, 64 focus groups, project visits, aid-worker survey, SMS survey, and secondary analysis.
limitations: Low SMS response, restricted Marib and de facto authority access, agency data-sharing constraints, and no climate-specific evaluation design. The final report is dated 13/14 July 2022; the WFP publisher page is dated 7 December 2022.

title: Yemen Emergency Crisis Response Project P159053: Implementation Completion Report Review
geographic_coverage: Yemen, project areas and participating local institutions
temporal_coverage: Emergency project implementation and completion through 2022.
methodology: Independent desk review of completion evidence, monitoring, third-party verification, outputs, and stated outcomes.
limitations: Welfare effects and causal mechanisms were inadequately specified, and output delivery is stronger evidence than sustained resilience.

title: Final Evaluation: Strengthening Institutional and Economic Resilience in Yemen
organization: United Nations Development Programme and European Union external evaluation team
methodology: External mixed-method evaluation with document review, 105 stakeholders, site evidence, and qualitative assessment.
limitations: No structured impact assessment or counterfactual; maintenance, inclusion, and peace effects remain incompletely measured.

title: Conflict Resilience of Water and Energy Supply Infrastructure: Insights from Yemen
geographic_coverage: Urban Yemen, including Sana'a and Taiz
methodology: Qualitative resilience framework using interviews, narratives, utility information, and secondary data.
limitations: Limited representativeness and incomplete quantitative data; continuity is not consistent system performance. Reuse terms: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0.

title: Livelihood Resilience and Adaptation Practices Among Agricultural Communities in Yemen
geographic_coverage: Six rural study areas in Abyan, Hadramawt, Marib, and Taiz
methodology: Purposive survey of 164 people, 20 interviews, six focus groups, ethnographic observation, and grounded-theory analysis.
limitations: Non-representative local sample, only 13 survey respondents in Marib, and causal claims rely heavily on perceptions and qualitative evidence. The PDF is publicly downloadable and copyrighted by the Sana'a Center, but no permissive reuse licence was identified.

title: Undercurrents: How Conflict, Climate Change and the Environment Intersect in Yemen
organization: adelphi research and the European Institute of Peace, under the Weathering Risk Peace Pillar
temporal_coverage: Primary fieldwork in 2023–2024 and reported conditions/cases through 2024.
methodology: Mixed methods: 2,283 survey respondents, 69 focus-group participants and 58 interviews across nine governorates.
limitations: Security constrained access; comprehensive climate data and projections were lacking. Cases are not nationally representative estimates.

title: UNDP Yemen: Building Resilience: Supporting Farmers to Face the Impact of Climate Change in Yemen
organization: United Nations Development Programme, published by United Nations in Yemen
temporal_coverage: FSRRP implementation and farmer accounts reported in March 2024, with project photos dated 2023.
methodology: UNDP project feature using named farmer and implementing-partner accounts and reported project outputs.
limitations: Programme reporting and attributed testimony, not an independent impact evaluation; no comparison group is provided.

title: From Seasonal to Sustainable: Year-Round Farming
organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
temporal_coverage: FAO-supported Shibam interventions and farmer accounts reported in February 2026.
methodology: FAO feature story based on project implementation and local farmer accounts in Shibam.
limitations: Project feature, not an independent evaluation; outcomes are reported by FAO and participants.

title: Addressing Community Needs While Redressing the Impact of Climate Change in Yemen
organization: United Nations Development Programme, Regional Bureau for Arab States
temporal_coverage: SIERY project implementation and local authority actions reported in April 2025.
methodology: UNDP project feature describing local-authority investments and reported programme outputs.
limitations: Promotional implementation account; it provides no independent impact design and some metrics lack denominators or baselines.

title: Cluster Evaluation of FAO Resilience Activities in Yemen 2018–2024
organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), Office of Evaluation
temporal_coverage: FAO resilience activity period 2018–2024; date of the evaluation webpage not stated.
methodology: FAO publisher-page summary of a cluster evaluation covering water-focused natural-resource management, agriculture, livestock and governance under the HDP nexus.
limitations: Only the official webpage summary was accessible; the linked report returned 403 and its local detail was not verified.
